relations.evidence: Use `upsert` rather than `insert` to upload the document even if the target key already has a value. This means that in the case of any error, it's easy to make any required tweaks to the import file and re-run the whole import.

notable_absence.finding: No role, privilege, or edition gate is mentioned anywhere on this page - access is governed entirely by whatever SDK connection credentials are used ('Administrator'/'password' in the worked examples), and the guide never states that Data Writer or any other capella-role is needed for SDK-scripted import, in contrast to capella:import-tool (round 7), which explicitly requires the Data Writer role. This is a genuine gap worth flagging: the same underlying action (writing documents into a bucket/scope/collection) is presented with an explicit role requirement via the UI path but no stated requirement via the SDK path on this page - plausibly because SDK connections are assumed to already be scoped by cluster access credentials rather than capella-roles, but the guide does not say so explicitly.

cross_component_finding: This directly answers the round's question about import.md/load.md revealing new content: import.md is genuinely new task-level territory, not duplicated from capella:data-api (round 6) or capella:import-tool (round 7). It documents a third, distinct import path - writing your own SDK client loop (parse CSV/TSV/JSON/JSONL with a language-native library, connect to the cluster, determine a document key, then call the SDK's upsert operation) - shown in four parallel SDK tabs (.NET, Java, Node.js, Python). Round 6's Data API is an HTTP passthrough for the Query/Search services and is not mentioned at all on this page; round 7's Import tool is mentioned only once as the UI alternative. No overlap or inconsistent duplication was found because the three paths (UI tool / Data API / SDK script) are non-overlapping in this page's own framing.
cross_product_finding: The four SDK code tabs (.NET, Java, Node.js, Python) demonstrate the same seven-step workflow (parse -> connect -> resolve bucket/scope/collection -> determine key -> preprocess -> upsert) using different third-party libraries per language (CsvHelper/Newtonsoft for .NET, opencsv/built-in JSON for Java including a Reactor reactive-API variant, csv-parse/stream-json for Node.js, csv/json for Python) - this is a single underlying import-workflow concept (sdk:bulk-import-workflow) expressed identically in shape across languages, similar to the one-concept/many-vocabularies pattern already flagged for CAS/ETag and for QueryOptions parameter-binding methods elsewhere in this batch.
